name: Liquid-nitrogen quick freezing of 'Northcountry' blueberries at -80, -100 and -120 °C to below Tg' (-52.55 °C), compared with a -80 °C ultra-low freezer
plain_name: Flash-freeze blueberries in liquid nitrogen to keep them firm and juicy
description: Blueberries were frozen to their glass-transition end point (Tg' = -52.55 °C) either in an ultra-low temperature freezer at -80 °C or by direct immersion in liquid nitrogen at set points of -80, -100 and -120 °C; LN-120 °C gave the least quality loss (juice loss, hardness, anthocyanin, membrane integrity, microstructure).
keywords: Flash-freeze blueberries in liquid nitrogen to keep them firm and juicy

sources.citation: Huang B, Li Y, Hu Z (2024). Effect of Glassy State and Liquid Nitrogen Quick Freezing on the Quality Characteristics of Blueberries. Food Science 45(6):225-232. doi:10.7506/spkx1002-6630-20230629-236

requirements.rationale: The best-performing treatment, LN-120 °C, needs the freezing space at -120 °C (153.15 K).
Freezing is done by direct immersion in liquid nitrogen.
Tg' (-52.55 °C = 220.6 K) is the freezing end point, so the machine must reach below it.
Reproducing the full comparison needs set points from -120 °C to -80 °C (153.15-193.15 K); optional beyond the -120 °C operating point.
The fruit is immersed directly in liquid nitrogen; supporting flag only.

confirmation_note: Requirements taken from the cited procedure and independently re-verified against the source (research/v4, 2026-11-01). Users must confirm them for their own run; edits require confirmation again.
